desc:
You are given a binary string s of length n (0-indexed). Two kinds of operations are available:

  • pick an index i and flip every character from index 0 to i inclusive, at a cost of i + 1;
  • pick an index i and flip every character from index i to n - 1 inclusive, at a cost of n - i.

Flipping turns '0' into '1' and '1' into '0'. Return the minimum total cost to make all characters of s equal (all zeros or all ones, whichever is cheaper).

For example, s = "0011" costs 2 (flip the first two characters, or the last two), and s = "010101" costs 9.
constraints: s contains only the characters '0' and '1'
hints: Look at the positions where two neighbours differ, i.e. s[i-1] != s[i]. If there are none, the answer is 0.
Each such boundary has to be removed. A boundary between index i-1 and i can be removed by flipping the whole prefix [0, i-1] (cost i) or the whole suffix [i, n-1] (cost n - i).
The boundaries can be handled independently: sum min(i, n - i) over all indices i with s[i-1] != s[i].
editorial: Only the boundaries between different neighbours matter. Flipping a prefix or a suffix changes the equal/different relation of exactly one pair of neighbours: the pair at the cut (all other pairs are flipped together and keep their relation). So each boundary needs its own operation, and the only operations that fix the boundary between indices i-1 and i are the prefix flip ending at i-1 (cost i) and the suffix flip starting at i (cost n - i).

Whichever flips we make, every boundary is fixed independently, and a cut at a place that is not a boundary would create a new one, so it never helps. Therefore the cost is the sum over boundaries of min(i, n - i). When all pairs are equal, the characters are equal, so we are done. Time O(n), space O(1).
